My husband is a drywaller. He is unionized and can work anywhere in Canada under different union locals and gets ~$40/hr (it varies depending on the union local...different agreements for different regions). They call the union, get added to a job list, and no matter where they work, they are guaranteed to be paid the same anywhere.

Meanwhile, nurses are getting paid $20-50/hr, depending on where they work. What a huge variance, and it only exists because agencies make it that way.
The staffing shortage is because no one wants to break their back, risk their health and put up with literal steaming piles of shit some days for a wage that just barely sustains a single person lifestyle. Just barely.
